system.name: FleetIO
system.one_liner: a learning-based storage virtualization framework that uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to balance performance isolation and utilization for shared SSDs

content.key_idea: Software-defined flash lets an SSD's channels and chips be virtualized into vSSDs, shareable with weak but high-utilization software isolation or dedicated with strong but low-utilization hardware isolation.
content.reading_order: Left panel shows how vSSDs map onto channels and flash chips; right panel contrasts vSSDs sharing a channel (software-isolated) with vSSDs that each own one (hardware-isolated).

summary: FleetIO is a learning-based storage virtualization framework that uses reinforcement learning to manage virtualized SSDs, aiming to achieve both performance isolation and high utilization on shared flash storage. This background figure, not FleetIO's own design, motivates the problem: panel (a) shows SSD virtualization with software-defined flash (SDF), where multiple vSSDs sit above an SSD Virtualization layer that maps them onto flash channels, each channel containing a flash controller and several flash chips capable of issuing I/O independently. Panel (b) contrasts the two existing isolation approaches collocating vSSDs on a shared SSD: vSSD-1 and vSSD-2 are software-isolated, mapped to the same flash channels and separated only by I/O throttling, which maximizes utilization but offers weak isolation; vSSD-3 and vSSD-4 are hardware-isolated, each fully owning its own dedicated channels for strong isolation at the cost of utilization. This isolation-versus-utilization tension motivates FleetIO's RL-based design shown in later figures.
summary_zh: 该背景图展示SSD虚拟化与隔离方式：(a)多个vSSD经虚拟化层映射到闪存通道与芯片；(b)对比软件隔离(共享通道，靠限流隔离，利用率高但弱隔离)与硬件隔离(独占通道，强隔离但利用率低)。
